clue.text: Lurches away from the mess

definitions.meaning: to walk off with an awkward, shuffling, lurching gait
a scene of total disorder or chaos

explanation.surface: Someone staggers out of the army dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means walks off clumsily and unsteadily; the noun means a scene of chaotic disorder, originally a slaughterhouse.

clue.text: Given bearing at head of lake, cast off

indicators.note: at head of puts the bearing in front of the lake word

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
a lough is an Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: A ship takes a southerly course from the top of a lake after leaving its mooring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is a link word. LOUGH is the Irish lake (as in Lough Neagh); 'at head of' sets S before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake can slough its skin, shedding or discarding it.

clue.text: A race has to finish, so take heed

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
end is a synonym of finish

explanation.surface: Every race must reach its conclusion, so pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' and 'so' are link words joining wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to something is to pay careful attention or listen closely.

clue.text: Pirate gang carrying equipment

indicators.note: carrying means the gang word holds the equipment word within it

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
rig is gear or equipment

explanation.surface: A pirate crew hauling their gear about.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit or outlaw, a robber who preys on travellers, close kin to a pirate.

clue.text: We take turn and turn about in jug

indicators.note: take here means accept something after it, joining the two parts
turn tells us to reverse the word we
the second turn reverses the short word meaning about

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: We share the job of pouring, swapping each time at the jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn and turn about' looks like the idiom for taking turns; instead each 'turn' reverses a piece: WE gives EW, and RE (about) gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed pitcher used for carrying water.

clue.text: Struck, and carried away, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for carried away is to be taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: rapt means enraptured or carried away

explanation.surface: Hit, and then swept off in a frenzy, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapped is the past tense of rap, to hit or knock sharply.

clue.text: Charge increased when battery included

parts.note: a criminal charge that becomes the heavier legal pairing with battery when that offence is added; battery here is the crime, not an electric cell

explanation.surface: An electrical charge rises once a battery is fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about electricity; in law, the charge gets more serious when battery (unlawful physical contact) is added to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Assault is a legal charge of threatening or attacking someone, commonly joined with battery.

clue.text: Mine-camp cooking provides survival rations

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters of mine-camp are being worked up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The cook at a mining camp prepares emergency food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges the eight letters of MINECAMP; 'provides' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pemmican is dried pounded meat mixed with fat, a compact food carried by explorers for survival.

clue.text: Taken out of oneself and re-channelled

definitions.meaning: entertained or amused, so distracted from one's troubles
sent along a different route or course

explanation.surface: Someone lifted from self-absorption and given a new outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused or entertained, so distracted from one's worries; also redirected, as traffic or a river sent another way.

clue.text: Got on it — a bed collapsed

indicators.note: collapsed suggests on it a bed falling down into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Climbed onto it, and the bed gave way.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtained is a synonym of acquired or procured.

clue.text: Rebuffed visa holding award winning novelist

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests something pushed back, so the whole is read backwards
holding means the visa word contains the award

parts.note: taken as written
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A celebrated author has a visa application turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'award' is not part of the definition: the Order of Merit is a British honour. 'Rebuffed' reverses the whole container, so the visa reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a science-fiction writer who won several Hugo and Nebula prizes.

clue.text: Pollutes the gorges

definitions.meaning: narrow passes or ravines through hills

explanation.surface: Someone dumps rubbish in mountain ravines.
explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to sully or desecrate; a defile is also a narrow mountain pass, so plural ravines.

clue.text: Cordial made from bottled spirit and some ale

annotationWithheld.why: Cordial made from bottled spirit and some ale (6): GENIAL; no sound parse found for GENI from 'bottled spirit' (GENIE gives one letter too many) and no source gives the setter's parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Cordial made from bottled spirit and some ale

clue.text: Odd pence, with some other money given to one we can't trust

parts.note: the ecu was the European currency unit, a foreign money
a liar is someone not to be trusted

explanation.surface: Unusual change: a penny plus foreign coins handed to a con man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'given to' are link words stringing the three pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar is a synonym of strange or unusual.

clue.text: Limit first class travel for these troops

indicators.note: travel suggests the letters moving around into a new order

parts.note: A1 means first class; the 1 is read as letter I

explanation.surface: A rule capping first-class journeys for soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a standard expression for first-rate; its 1 becomes I, and 'travel' rearranges LIMIT plus AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of citizen soldiers, a force of part-time troops.

clue.text: Relay teams I'd train to run

indicators.note: to run suggests the letters of teams I'd train getting going in a new order

explanation.surface: Coaching sprint relay squads for a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to dispense or pass on, as one relays something to others.

clue.text: With light admission of being puffed out, embracing little old woman

indicators.note: embracing means the puffed-out word wraps around the abbreviations

parts.note: winded means out of breath, puffed out
O and W are the short forms of old and woman

explanation.surface: Breathless, someone confesses while hugging a tiny elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admission' looks like a confession but belongs to the definition: letting light in. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A windowed room has glazed openings that let daylight into it.

clue.text: Broken step made for unstable flight

indicators.note: broken suggests step made smashed and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A broken stair made for a rickety staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like a set of stairs; it is a panicked rush. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden uncontrolled rush of panicking animals or people.

clue.text: Spy reports clientele tipsy with gin?

indicators.note: tipsy suggests the letters of clientele and gin staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: An agent notes that the bar's customers are drunk on gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence is secret information gathered by espionage agents.

clue.text: Five-year craving for strong drink

parts.note: lust is a strong craving
rum is a strong spirit

explanation.surface: Half a decade of longing for hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum is a period of five years, from a Roman purification held every five years.

clue.text: Vineyard is presented to her majesty by privateer

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A privateer hands a vineyard over to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented to' and 'by' are link words setting the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is an armed ship; a privateer was a privately owned warship licensed to raid.

clue.text: Farewell is interrupted in this case

indicators.note: interrupted means the farewell word is broken into by is

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

explanation.surface: A goodbye cut short in this situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in this' are link words; 'case' looks like a situation but is luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a small travelling bag or suitcase.

clue.text: A number turn up to do mischief? It's just a game

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: turn up in a down entry means read the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: Ten people arrive to cause trouble, but it's only a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's just a' are link words leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net.

clue.text: Daily, ordered items c o d

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters of items c o d put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A list of goods bought cash on delivery each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like an adverb; it is a British word for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant, and a daily is a cleaning woman who comes by day.

clue.text: Copper — it's invaluable — can be a paralysing poison

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rare means scarce and precious

explanation.surface: Copper, precious stuff, can be a deadly toxin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' and 'can be a' are link words; 'Copper' looks like a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant extract used on arrow tips that relaxes muscles to the point of paralysis.

clue.text: Having the last word, alter the title

indicators.note: alter suggests changing the word by moving its first letter to the back

parts.note: a name is a title

explanation.surface: Getting final say, someone changes the heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter' moves the N of NAME to the end; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen closes a prayer, the word said at the end in agreement.

clue.text: Query about blunder vessel made

indicators.note: about means the query word goes round the blunder word

parts.note: why is a question
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: Asking why a mistake has been made on the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or barge.

clue.text: Issue is in some confusion

indicators.note: confusion suggests the letters of is in some jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A problem is thrown into disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a matter for discussion; it means something given off.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is a discharge, something that flows out.

clue.text: Romantic girl, blushing at first

annotationWithheld.why: Romantic girl, blushing at first (6): DREAMY; girl AMY and blushing RED give RED before AMY (REDAMY), not D+RE+AMY, and no source gives the setter's parse.

clue.text: With their aid, start seeing snoek right and left, at sea?

indicators.note: start means take only the first letter of seeing
at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Divers spot a snoek fish swimming to either side while underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: A snoek is a South African fish. 'start' takes the S of seeing; 'at sea' rearranges SNOEK, R and L into NORKEL; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Snorkels are breathing tubes that let swimmers look underwater.
